mechanism_narrative: A higher Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reflects tighter monetary policy, increasing the cost of capital and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 5-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or correlation is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or mean return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect between INDPRO and UNRATE on 60-day SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.05), or Rank IC for joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rate hikes reduce liquidity and increase risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, or mean return in tightening cycles is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Higher residential construction activity (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST against 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or correlation is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 258.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting monetary tightening and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 258.0, or mean return in high-inflation periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) coupled with a rise in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced demand and tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect between RSAFS and FEDFUNDS on 60-day SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.05), or Rank IC for joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening regime (UNRATE < 3.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), strong employment boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, or mean return in tightening labor markets is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
